# Session Narrative — ray_molformer/20260725_000436

This session picked up a previously-stalled pipeline (2-node baseline + optimization round
completed 2026-07-25) and delivered the missing piece: a working 4-node/16-GPU baseline,
never before achieved for this app. Six real, previously-undiagnosed bugs were found and
fixed to get there (dataset/PFS symlinking, HF model cache location, a pinned HF revision
a plain download misses, a `transformers` dynamic-module concurrent-write race, a broken
Ray-join retry-loop success check, and dftracer's HIP-tracing init-ordering crash inside
Ray's `default_worker.py`).

With `baseline_4node` traced (12 iterations, exit 0, 27.3M events, all 9 categories
confirmed via direct chunk scan), the pipeline ran `dftracer-analyzer` then the full
4-dimension `dftracer-optimizer` dispatch (Pipeline Policy #14). The honest headline: two
applied compute variants (opt4, opt5) both measured null. The value of the round was three
diagnostic corrections instead of a speedup — disproving the "redundant HF model load"
hypothesis in favor of an immovable 58.9s `hipModuleLoad` cost, re-attributing 541.7s of
RCCL collective time that HIP tracing had hidden inside `kernel_dispatch`, and confirming
memory has no optimization target because zero checkpoint files are ever read.

This report agent then assembled `final_report/`, attempted to persist six approved
self-learning skill updates (blocked by worktree write isolation — see REPORT.md §11),
wrote a new memory entry for the confirmed `comparator` tool bug, and ran the mandatory
privacy scan before closing out.
